_notice: get_pilot_diagnostics is a Tauri #[tauri::command] reachable only via live frontend IPC (invoke('get_pilot_diagnostics')) from within a running webview. This container has no webview-automation tooling (no WebDriver/tauri-driver, no way to drive the actual React UI and read back an IPC response), so this file is NOT a captured live response and must not be read as one. It is a structural example: real field VALUES drawn from files this phase already produced honestly (machine.json, Xvfb run logs, manifest.json), assembled into the exact JSON SHAPE get_pilot_diagnostics actually serializes (see apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs, struct PilotDiagnostics and its field types), so a reviewer can see what the expanded diagnostics command now reports without a fabricated 'live capture' claim.
shapeSource: apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs: PilotDiagnostics { machine, whisperModel, audioDevices, audio, displays, bible, database }

whisperModel._note: real value from this container: no ggml/gguf model file is configured or present - see whisper-test.json

audio._note: real value from this container: /dev/snd does not exist, so cpal enumerates zero devices and the engine reports idle/no-device state - see audio-test.json and hardware-status.json

bible.name: Berean Standard Bible
bible._note: real value shape from docs/data/bible/BSB/manifest.json / content_registry, confirmed present after each Xvfb run this phase

database._note: real result of the non-mutating OpenOptions writable check against this container's Xvfb-run database file

realHardware.note: get_pilot_diagnostics has never been invoked from a real running webview on a real pilot machine. On real target hardware, whisperModel.status, audioDevices, audio, and displays above would report genuinely different values (a real model file or a real Missing/Unreadable result, real enumerated microphones, a real capturing/idle state, and the real monitor(s) actually connected) - none of that is known and none of it is guessed here.
